recs.name: One Should, One Must
recs.tag: No longer a shinobi, and no longer bound by devotion, but she long since pledged her loyalty to her current job.

lines.st: In the corner of every session is a figure with her head perpetually down, recording every word said by the City Council.

lines.x: January 1st, 10:12 A.M.
'We propose waiving the right to education for the Infected.'
'We propose imposing no limit on the hours an Infected can work, to ensure that they can earn as much as their ability allows, supporting their own livelihood.'
'We urge the Infected to wear special Infected clothing going forward...'
The silent recorder moves her sore wrists, turning to a new page in her notebook.
January 8th, 6:23 P.M.
'Councilor Jones objects, and proposes a new criteria for assigning jobs to the Infected...'
'Councilor Moneywell proposes a bill to limit the number of Infected factories can employ...'
Still busy, Kite?
Mhm...
Sorry to bother you, but may I ask... where exactly are those documents regarding the demolition of the factories in the east end filed? I can't find them at all.
Folder no.10289 in cabinet B03, third drawer behind the bookshelf.
Heh, I just knew you'd know where it was right away! If I had a head as good as yours, my mum would be so happy she'd slurp down three bowls of cheese soup at once!
Work hours are already over though, so why's your pen still moving...? Oh, Infected this, Infected that... my head hurts.

I already sent in an application; even if I'm just a receptionist for the council chamber, it'd still be better than being a filing clerk. This is just too boring! Why not try applying too, Kite? We can work there together.
What? No no no!
You don't know how hard I worked for this recorder job. My parents want me to be safe and secure, so keeping this position is the best for me. How could I even think of transferring?
Gosh, you're just too timid!
*sigh* Come on, just look at this pot of half-withered flowers I've been raising. Even if I were to change jobs, their situation probably wouldn't get any better.
My brain's good at rote memorization, so being a recorder suits me just fine.
January 15th, 11:45 A.M.
'We propose issuing a special series of banknotes for the Infected, to boost domestic demand...'
'We propose issuing half of the Infected's wages in the form of consumer vouchers...'
Phew......
Wait, I have one more bill to propose!
As I'm sure we all saw this morning, the protest march against Infected desegregation has become such a nuisance that it's even blocking the roads that some of us councilors take!
I was in a hurry and had to loudly heckle them several times to stop blocking my way to work, lest today's council session be delayed.
So I propose allowing the Infected to buy homes, what does everyone think?

If all those Infected workers had adequate housing, they would stop wandering about like vagrants looking for shelter. Then they wouldn't have any reason to interfere with the lives of ordinary people and spark such protests, yes?
Additionally, there are quite a number of Infected in Caladon these days. If each of them bought a house, imagine the boost to the economy!

Councilor Jones, I hear from the others that you've taken on the bid for that land development project on the east end, and they were all harping on about how it was a huge project that would take at least a decade to finish.
Hey now! That's all just hearsay, how could you possibly believe that... Besides, how could it be compared to the roadwork you're backing?
Once the roads are good as new, the people will get moving, and then anything and everything could happen, right?
Our city's development is progressing at a steady pace, but there's no place for such protests in our future. Just a few of us were delayed today, but who knows how much worse it could be tomorrow?
Keeping the general public of Caladon safe and earning their trust is our most basic responsibility.
Only once the residents are at ease can we think about developing our economy!
Recorder? Did you get all that down?
Yes, Miss Councilor.
So, what does everyone think? As soon as the road connecting to the east end is repaired, we can begin work on so many more projects!
...I have no particular opinion on this, but such a bill will be beneficial to everyone, so I will back your proposal.
Recorder, be sure to note every word of this down! The quicker we settle this, the better!
Got it, Councilor Jones.
Please hold on for a moment. I have something to say about the previous proposal.
I find myself curious. These Infected workers... would they even be able to afford a house?
Whyever not? They'll earn enough from the roadwork, and it'll all sort itself out.
January 15th, 6:12 P.M.
So, the good news is that the processing of both the business certificates and access permits the landship needs is going well, so you'll be able to get them all by the next month.
And the bad news is that in the six months since you last submitted a report, it's been long enough for them to finally make a little breakthrough on their proposed bills.
And this latest one is to 'let the Infected buy houses'?
Mhm.
...If I recall your last report correctly, you mentioned that there were a couple of bills proposed that were potentially beneficial for the Infected. What happened to those?
You can probably come up with an answer to that yourself, Captain.

The councilors feel that even though this one is the least feasible, it can still be taken advantage of. Whether it be by those holding vacant land, those with factories, or those repairing the roads, they all want a piece of the pie.
Now that the bill has already been placed on the cutting board, all that's left is to divide the pie to everybody's satisfaction.
The remaining proposals will be squished under the pie pan, and maybe trod upon a few more times for good measure.
...I know that much.
Recently, we've been admitting more Infected patients with acute symptoms.
I'm not complaining, but... things are getting harder for us, even with all the material support we're getting from the landship.
And there will only be more such patients in the future.
That said... the certificates and permits you're getting us will give us more options. So we might still have some tricks up our sleeve going forward.
But... gah! Do you know what kind of Infected we've been admitting this month? Children!
Our efforts will be for naught if they keep screwing around in their City Council sessions like this!
...But we can't interfere, right?
Yes, generally speaking.
Captain, what do you think about Skyfire?
Why bring her up all of a sudden?
Oh, I was just... I think she comes from a good background, and has a good heart, but her worldview is still a little small.
She listens to reason, but has never had to experience reality, so she used an improper method to deal with those councilors when she found out how they really are.
If not for Councilor Angst, or her identity as a Mountbelan, those nobles probably would have served her a lesson—both overt and covert—and forced her out of Caladon in disgrace.
Sometimes she disagrees with my methods too. I'll always choose to preserve my status as a City Council recorder first, mindlessly nodding my head and noting down whatever the councilors say.
Only occasionally do I bring you the evidence they leave behind to make some use out of it.
I always thought her way of charging into things head-on was no good, but—
She's never made an error, and never forgets it: what she does is right. She has never relented on this.
We all have our own ways of upholding justice, Kazemaru.
Hah... But the councilors usually take no notice of me. They don't even remember my name.
They just go 'Recorder, record this,' 'Recorder, take that down.' They probably wouldn't even notice if I changed into a completely different person one day.
Kazemaru, we can't interfere with the council.
I used to chide Skyfire for that too, saying she shouldn't do such a rash thing.
...You know your limits.
Of course I do. So I'm going to pack up my things and go back to the archives and continue sorting through the files.
Oh right, these are the little paper animals I folded. You can give them to the younger Infected to play with.
Now that's more like it. Don't look so sad, we're still hanging in there. We'll manage to figure something out.
...Wait, why do these look so much rougher than the ones from last time?
Look at this horn, it's all twisted! It better not turn into a one-winged fowlbeast when I give it to a kid later!
...I'm going now!
*sigh*
January 17th, 7:19 A.M.
Early day today, Kite?
A new batch of documents arrived, so I'm sorting and filing them...
Oh, I heard you got transferred to the front desk? Congrats!
Heheh, it's my last day today here, so I'll help you out!

Let me tell you, I was passing by the council room yesterday, and I heard them argue about whether to raise the tax rate to limit the Infected's quality of life... even I thought that was a bit of a joke.
Yeah.
January 22nd, 7:32 A.M.
'We propose deducting 30% of the Infected's wages as a reparations fee, to pay for the damages caused to the city by the Infected.'
'We propose following Columbia's example, for the wilderness has vast acres of untapped resources with which the Infected may live prosperous lives.'
The recorder in the corner puts down her pen and, as if having gotten dust on them, wipes her hands vigorously with a handkerchief from her pocket before throwing it into the nearby trashcan.
...Ssh!
What's wrong with you? Don't make so much noise all of a sudden! Don't recorders know such a basic rule?
...My apologies, Councilor Jones.
I will make sure to stay quiet.
January 27th, 6:42 P.M.
'We will continue to push for the bill to let the Infected buy housing...'
'We expect it to be implemented by next year...'
The recorder organizes the documents, carefully filing them into their respective envelopes, and writes the date on the label before placing them into the filing cabinet.
There is a thin layer of dust on top of the cabinet, and she picks up a rag and wipes it.
She turns to her desk and begins to tidy up the area—the Records Room is packed with people looking for information during the day, and keeping the desk neat and tidy is also part of her disguise.
A potted flower sits on the corner of the desk, its petals drooping.
*crash*—!
An unstable flower pot is buffeted by the wind and falls from the sky, throwing streaks of soil and scattering petals everywhere.
The clay pot falls straight down with the mud and hits a young woman just passing by square on her head.
She does not let out any kind of cry after her collision, but simply touches the mud on her face in a daze.
The recorder looks at the pot of dropping flowers on her desk, which she had just tended to earlier, and finds its position perfectly secure.
She stretches a hand out.
*crash*—!
January 27th, 10:39 P.M.
Aaaahhhhhh—!!
What was that?! Did you hear that? Was that even human? That gave me a real fright!
The whole of Caladon probably heard that scream.
It sounded like it came from the villas. Maybe the nobles are playing around with some new toys again.
Whew, that ding dong clanging sure sounded like someone waltzing around with furniture strapped onto their back!
Haha, a waltz with furniture? How posh!

Ten minutes ago, Councilor Jones had been lounging comfortably on his sofa, sipping the wine his servants had prepared for him. Their backs blended into the light, while the shadows of his guards were reflected at his feet.
In Caladon, such an arrangement allows him to enjoy many a perfectly peaceful night in his mansion.
But few things are absolute.
Ah—Ahh—!
What is this, what's happening?!
The books on the shelf and the medals on the wall all stand up, taking even the bookshelf straight towards the couch where the councilor is lounging.
As if alive, a bunch of paper folds itself, becoming tiny figures, mouths, sharp knives.
They swirl around the confused councilor—
Help! Someone, help! What's all this!
My books? My... files? They're alive!
The paper dolls vibrate in mid-air, and tiny voices seep out from the words written on them—
'We urge the Infected to wear special Infected clothing going forward!'
'We propose issuing a special series of banknotes for the Infected, to boost domestic demand!'
'Let them buy housing? Yes, of course! Let them buy houses, we have many uses for the Infected!'
Ahhh!!! What's going on, someone! Anyone? Guards? Guards!
'Cystymilk is delicious, and we should increase our supply! The Infected—'
'The Infected should pay a reparations fee! We propose issuing half of the Infected's wages in the form of consumer vouchers!'
What are these! Get, get away from me!
The Councilor falls to the ground on his back, flailing his hands in an attempt to drive away the paper dolls encircling him.
He picks up a wine glass, aiming its contents at a paper doll. The wine seeps into the paper, and the swirl of white turns red as it fills the room with an alcoholic aroma.
Head in hands, the councilor huddles in a corner of the room, leaving only his rotund backside shaking in view.
Ah! Ahh!! AHHH!!
The paper dolls continue to close in on him, the overlapping voices encircling the Councilor.
Who are you? What do you want?!
W-What, what do you want from me?!
I'll do anything you ask! Anything! Let me go, just let me go, please?!
As if they had gotten what they wanted, the paper dolls stop spinning around the councilor and instead hover quietly.
Then, they stretch out their bodies, reverting to their original sheets of paper before landing on the ground. The councilor panics and crumples them, afraid that they might once again take flight.
In the midst of the flurry, a document lands quietly on the middle of his desk.
His hands trembling, Councilor Jones picks it up—
'Report on the City's East End Development Project'...?

After glancing at the open document for just a few seconds, the councilor crumples it into a ball with a twisted expression on his face. He is about to throw it into the trash, but hesitantly smooths it out instead, folds it, and carefully places it in his inner coat pocket.
This... What is this doing here...? Who found this? Didn't I already...
Sir... did you call for me? Should I come in and help you clean up?
You dolt! What are you standing outside for!
R-Right away!
Wait... No! No need!
Out! Get out! Get away from here, now!
The councilor bends down and scrambles to gather the papers scattered on the floor, fearfully scanning the heading and contents of each sheet, as if afraid to see something else on them.
He looks around, wary of the entire room. He then pulls back the curtains with a flourish.
Someone is definitely behind this! And he's going to find out who!
Ah, if it isn't Councilor Jones? Still at work at such a late hour, tidying up your papers?
You?!

(Loudly) I expected no less of you, Councilor Jones! To still be hard at work sorting through your files at such a late hour, polishing your proposal into an even better bill to better serve everyone!
(Loudly) I just now finished discussing the east end factory with the Infected representative earlier, and he's so grateful to see you working so hard for the council!
(Loudly) Truly a councilor who looks after the Infected! Come come, representative, you must thank him in person!
Truly, thank you so much, Councilor Jones! Our brothers in the factories will surely remember you for this!
...Haha, hahaha.
Y-Yes, yes! Haha...!
February 3rd, 9:19 P.M.
Councilor Jones, withdrawing a proposal is unprecedented. Do you realize what your actions are implying?
Everyone here has been working hard on their own preparations these last few days, all based on that proposal.
...No, I'm saying... I... I want to withdraw that bloody proposal!
Please forgive me, I... I've come to my senses over the last few days. This was a foolish idea.
Councilor Jones, the City Council is no place for playing around. Perhaps if you told us of any difficulties you've encountered recently, we might be able to help you.
No! Nothing of the sort!
Recorder? Recorder, are you there? Kite, Kite! Quick, note down my decision to withdraw the proposal! And file it! Quickly!
The recorder clicks her pencil, and as per her usual, writes down every word from the session in her minutes.
Got it, Councilor Jones.
February 7th, 3:18 P.M.
What a pity I went home early that night. Who would've expect something like that to happen in Councilor Jones's own home?
I've heard others say that the house was completely fine, but suddenly the stationery started moving and dancing. It could even speak!
Here are the business certifications and permits. You can return to the landship now, captain.
Good job on your end, too.
I heard his servants say that the councilor was frightened by something, but he didn't let them or even his guards enter the room. He tidied up his room himself!

I also heard that ever since that day, the Jones family has forbidden the use of paper, saying that some kind of foul evil lies within, haha! Then, how do you think he does his business in the loo...?
Seems like they're talking about what happened to Councilor Jones the other day? News spreads so fast, doesn't it?
...*cough*!
Hey, enough about this, the captain's still hard at work so we should be too!
Kazemaru.
Did you...?
Captain, do you have the inside story? Share it with us, we won't tell a soul!
Ssh.

recs.name: In a Crowd
recs.tag: In the crowd, behind her back, the seeds she sowed have begun to bear fruit.

lines.st: We're holding a feast to celebrate the end of the war! Everyone in the city is invited!

lines.x: The war's finally over! We lived through it!
Hahahaha, now we get to eat every day! Bread, steak, and clean new clothes on the daily!
Whoa there, keep waving your arms like that and my stew's going to the floor—
Careful! Let me help you.
Oh dear, girlie. Where did you come from? Didn't see you in here till now.
Though, you did save my stew. Thank you.
Maybe because I was behind you the whole time? But take your time, okay? I'll help you serve it.
Alright. Thank you, dearie.
My pleasure. I know you've been buying medicine for the Infected and have even come to help cook today, so this is the least I could do.
The old woman smiles, and reaches out to tuck stray strands of hair back under her headband.
Ooh, that hairband of yours is so pretty.
Really? I'm glad you think so—I made it myself.
(Phew, did I subconsciously go all stealth-mode earlier? Good thing I didn't give her a fright.)
(Now I should hurry and distribute the stew.)
Oho! Look! Another dish for our table!
Come on now, lass, you've worked enough. Sit down and eat with us!
Hear, hear! We even have red wine!
Sure thing.
Brother, I'd like to make a toast to you! Gotta thank you for helping me decorate the shop a few days back. Would've taken days more doing it alone.
Hah! That was nothing. Didn't your family share all those fruits with mine back then? They filled my belly with hope for a better future. Just think of it as returning the favor.
And you, I have to thank you too, for helping us rent a car! Couldn't have even gotten our hands on those fruits and veg without that!
No, no, I hardly did a thing.
Haha, after going through those nightmarish days together, we'll be buddies forever! C'mon, everyone! Cheers!
(...My hard work wasn't in vain. That's great.)
Cheers—!
Huh? What's with the long face, gramps? Food not to your taste?
...No, the food is wonderful.
Maybe I'm just a little tired... haha.
No worries. Come on, let's have a drink together! A pint of our newest brew!
Best beer of my life!
My, my, boys! I know this is a celebration, but keep it down and try not to bother the neighbors, will you?
We should be more elegant, more 'Victorian' in our revelry! Here, a toast, with a precious vintage from my collection. Hahaha, it was worth it hiding it in the cellar!
Sounds great!
Let's have a toast then. I've never tried wine before!
The old man remains silent for a long time.
Before the smiles on their faces can be replaced with doubt, the old man finally clinks his glass against the rest. He drinks the wine in one gulp, then immediately stands up.
Alright, I'm going.
But the joyful party-goers are reluctant to let him leave just like that.
Come on, we've still got more food on the way, and you're leaving already?
Just stay a while longer, old chap. Who else will enjoy this fine vintage after you're gone?
...I'm good.
Hey, just a little longer won't hurt, right?
Yeah, look...
Hey now, what if he's busy or something? No need to hold him up.
...Thanks.
Oh right, gramps. Where's that darling daughter of yours? Didn't bring her today?
Glass shatters as if a bomb was dropped, halting multiple conversations.
The boisterous banquet falls into a dead silence, and several people stare with shock at the broken shards on the floor.
My daughter is dead!
My little girl, who I looked after ever since she was born. Always a healthy one, and I never let her suffer even during the war. But, but...
But she died of acute Oripathy!
She had a wonderful life ahead of her! But now she's gone, while the Infected are allowed to sit here and eat with us?! Hah! Do you even care if you spread it to someone else?!
You, all of you, the Infected and those who allow them to live alongside you. I hate you all.
You'll all meet a wretched end, sooner or later.
...And that concludes my report on the party last night, Captain.
These past few days, we've been resettling the Infected, helping to rebuild damaged buildings, transporting supplies, and re-opening factories and shops.
Many Infected have volunteered and contributed to our efforts. Last night was a long-awaited party to celebrate the recent work done in Caladon.
...I just didn't expect that. Now I'm worried that anti-Infected sentiment will return unless we do something.
Based on our recent findings, many feel their quality of life hasn't increased since the war, but that the risk of contracting Oripathy has increased due to the growing number of the Infected.
Others have lost their family or friends to Oripathy, so the situation is... as expected, really.
I think we need to assign people to deal with this, Captain, or it might spiral out of control.
But we're already short on hands. Resettling injured Infected, post-war reconstruction work... There's still a lot to handle on our end too.
The best we can manage is to keep an ear to the ground. If you notice any conflict, contact the police right away, and give them your cooperation.
...Understood, Captain.
My next missions are... to visit privately opened classrooms, resettle the Infected, and organize files in Parliament...
I'll do my best.
(Schools have yet to reopen, and these ad-hoc classes have been going unreported to the government. But since they're run by actual school teachers, I guess it's fine.)
(Phew. The lesson's finally over. I'll head back and mark the mission as complete.)
...Hey, did you see it? The boy in front looks like an Infected.
Huh?
(I should follow them and see what's going on.)
Whoa, he sure does! Don't sit on any chairs he's been on, or you might catch it.
Man, the war's over, but with so many more Infected around all of a sudden, who's to say we won't catch it ourselves one day? Why don't the teachers separate us into different classes?
Your recovery's going well and your condition's stable. Look, we even found a place for you to reopen your business. You can start from selling some daily necessities here.
It's a good spot with plenty of foot traffic, so you won't go home empty handed. But remember to save your earnings. Don't worry about the medical bills, you can pay them when you've got extra money.
Alright. Thank you, really, I mean it!
Don't mention it.
This a shop? Can I get two bottles of water?
Coming right up, sir! Here you go!
—Wait! Y-Y-Your hands! Crystals?!
S-S-Stay the bloody hell away from me! I don't want these! And keep the cash! I didn't survive that entire war just to catch your sickness! ...What rotten luck.
Calm down, sir. Haven't you seen the government announcements? Oripathy doesn't spread through ordinary physical contact.
Hmph. Who cares what they say? I don't believe a word of it. Are they gonna help me if I get Infected later? Now go! Get far, far away from me!
One more, just one more...
And, and also...
(Is that the old lady from the other day?)
What are you doing tearing down this wall by yourself, ma'am?
Ma'am?
Haven't seen you around before, but this uniform... Are you from the government?
Yes, I work at the town archives. Here's my work pass.
Let me see... Looks like it's no lie! You people have been doing good work lately, so I'll talk.
The old woman stands up and points to a house surrounded by the wall.
Old Hamm's in there. A good man, and neighbor of mine for decades. We've always gotten along.
Don't know where those hooligans heard rumors about him being Infected, but they kept going on and on about how he'd infect us or whatnot, and that we should wall him in.
He didn't want to be a bother, though, so he just agreed. But I don't. He's been sick for so long, you know, and we used to have our meals together, and I haven't caught Oripathy from him, no.
Alright, that's enough from me. When my son gets back he'll probably try and stop me, saying we'll be shunned by our neighbors if I keep this up... My goodness...
I'll help you out.
Oh girlie... thank you so much. My eyes aren't so good anymore, but what's your name? I'll thank you at your workplace someday.
It's fine, you don't have to know who I am. I'm just someone who wants to help.
...That'll do. Alright, let's hurry and get this over with so Old Hamm can get some sunlight again!
Mum!
Gah, speak of the Feline...
Didn't we talk about this, Mum? Stop knocking at that wall already! Old Hamm's not even bothered by it, so why are you?
What if they come after our family instead? You're too old to be causing a ruckus like this. Come on, let's go home!
*sigh*...
And you. Why were you helping this stubborn old woman instead of stopping her?
Just go already!
Kazemaru sighs and puts down the brick in her hand as she watches the man escort his mother home.
The wall still stands, as if no matter how hard she or the old woman tried, it would remain standing for all time.
She suddenly feels her shoulders ache.
She has not felt this in ages; not even the brutal physical training from her days as a ninja left her this exhausted.
We've done so much...
So why does it feel like we haven't done a thing?
Kazemaru, stop whatever you're doing and return to the office, pronto.
A large crowd of worked up people are outside our doors demanding we hand over our Infected patients!
One particularly angry one keeps saying his daughter died from acute Oripathy!
Get all those Infected out here!
Don't be rash now. I doubt anyone here was responsible for your daughter's death. They're just ordinary patients we've verified the identities of...
Aren't those 'ordinary patients' Infected? Won't they pass it on to others?
How many people have they spread their illness to and killed? Why do they get to live in peace, without taking any responsibility?
We're a pharmaceutical company, sir. I'm in charge here, and I can assure you none of their conditions are contagious—
No! You're not pulling the wool over my eyes! Can you take responsibility for my daughter's death?!
Can you?! Huh?!
Exactly!
The war's over, and everyone's suffering. No one gives a crap about us common folk, yet there's a entire company giving special treatment to the Infected?!
Free treatment, free jobs! But what about the rest of us? Are you saying it's fine if we get Infected too?!
Every Infected ought to leave Caladon!
The rowdy residents shout and yell, but no one makes a move, merely egging each other on.
(Whispering) Kazemaru, keep your face down, and do your best to... try and disperse the crowd.
...Understood.
Hey! Who's he talking to?
What're you trying to pull, huh? Calling the reporters? The coppers?
We just want these sick people to leave and prevent any more of us from getting Infected. What's wrong with that?
Everyone, please calm down. Like the government has been announcing, most Infected are unable to casually spread their Oripathy to others...
We don't have to go back to how it was a few years ago...
(Loudly) Yeah, no one cares about us normal folks anyways! Just yesterday I was next to an Infected, and I said 'If you're sick, then you shouldn't be mingling in public!'
(Loudly) Why is that so hard to understand?! Who knows if he could infect me, right? And then you know what? He launched a fireball at me before I could get another word in!
The Infected may occasionally lose control of their Originium Arts, but they don't do it on purpose...
(Loudly) He missed, but it freaked me out! What's worse, none of those sickos even bothered to see if I was hurt! Instead they went and asked if that Infected was alright!
(Loudly) I just wanted him to stay away from me, and he tried to attack me?! Did I deserve that, huh?!
Ugh...
Kazemaru tries to come up with the words, but fails, not knowing how to even react.
It seems this group will refuse to hear her out no matter what she tries.
Infiltration, tracking, and baiting enemies come as naturally to her as breathing, but now she merely stands rooted to the spot, frozen amongst the crowd—
While the crowd still watches and waits, biding their next chance to tear into her, to vent their suppressed emotions.
*thump*! *thump*! *thump* *thump* *thump* *thump* ...!
A sound suddenly emerges from the crowd.
An ignorant child, blissfully unaware of what the adults were doing, was merely playing with a ball when it slipped out of his hand and rolled onto the path.
Ah, my ball!
'Scuse me, 'scuse me! My ball rolled over there!
The child yells as he dives into the crowd.
The noisy crowd falls silent for a moment.
Kazemaru suddenly grows nervous.
...Hey, did you see under his sleeves? Aren't those black bits Originium crystals?
Looks like it. I've seen that kid before. His mum brought him along for a medicine run, which they got in a black bag. That's how Infected medicine usually gets packed.
'Scuse me, 'scuse me! I saw my ball roll over here!
...Where's his parents? Why aren't they here for him?
Hmph, who knows? Maybe they're Infected too, and are too afraid to come!
Gah, where's my ball?
I lost it? But how?
Ah, he's rolling up his sleeves!
Look! He's an Infected!
Grab him!
Get out of Caladon, Infected!
(Go, my paper dolls!)
Wha?!
Where'd you come from? Are you blind?!
He clearly remembers reaching out to grab the Infected child. But now, he suddenly bumps into a stranger, and accidentally tears something off their arm.
He looks up to see the strange arm missing a chunk, but looks back down to see it in his grasp—
Paper?
That guy earlier... was made of paper?!
Paper?
What's going on?! Let me see!
Hey! Where did you come from? And what's that on you?
Say something!

A few days later
'This report summarizes the recent situation in Caladon. We witnessed a relatively threatening anti-Infected rally.'
'But with help from the police and several anonymous residents, the unrest was quickly quelled.'
'The city council has also received the new Infected bill and is redesigning the city quarters to ensure the Infected and non-Infected will be able to live in peace together.'
Her report complete, Kazemaru pauses for a thought.
'Though we have encountered many difficulties, there are many more besides us who are also doing their best to prevent the situation from worsening.'
'Some frustration is inevitable, but as long as we persevere, the situation will definitely improve.'
Kazemaru puts down her pen, folds the report, and slots it into an envelope. She then quickly changes into her recorder outfit and walks out the door.
She feels as if she is experiencing the long-lost feeling of being a ninja.
In fact, she is no longer operating solo. Around her are many other 'ninjas', with hidden names and identities, who have been working in silence to turn things for the better.
She looks toward the government building not too far away. Caladon's city council is about to hold a special meeting soon.
'However, we will need a little more time to handle this.'
